Olivia K: Quick update — ran full bring-up for athena-9b this morning. Float16 vs int8 vs int6. Int6 is tempting on cost/latency but we see consistent recall drops on long-context QA slices. Looking for a practical handoff for GTN/product: safe defaults, canary plan, and fallback rules.

Samir P: Raw bench numbers to start: p95 token latency f16=120ms, int8=88–95ms, int6=70–75ms. Tokens/sec per GPU: f16~600, int8~820, int6~1020. Estimated cost per 1M tokens: f16=$28, int8=$18, int6=$11. Quality on our long-QA dev slice (ROUGE-L): f16=72.1, int8=71.0, int6=66.2. So int6 buys ~38% cost reduction vs f16 but drops ROUGE-L ~6 pts on long context. Problem areas: coreference, multi-step math, citation presence.

Dena L: Product perspective: we need defaults that keep customer-facing QA/research features high precision. My suggestion: default to int8 for chat & important QA paths; enable int6 only for short completions (<100 tokens) and low-risk surfaces (typeahead, inline suggestions). Route long-form or precision-critical queries to f16 or larger-model float16 fallback. Canary plan: 3% traffic, slice-based gating (queries >200 tokens OR contains tokens like 'calculate', 'cite', 'evidence'). Monitor quality deltas at slice level.

Samir P: Implementation caveats: int6 shows slightly different KV-cache alignment and we saw ~5% worse effective cache reuse on prefix-heavy flows — that hurts long chat. Also tokenization edge cases: some prompts produce length delta leading to perf variance. We'll need a small microbench for KVCACHE before broad rollout.

Olivia K: Can we encode a simple routing config for infra to try? e.g. rule-based routing plus canary tag.

Samir P: here's a minimal example to start with — use as a pilot routing policy in Redwood routing layer:
```yaml
routes:
  - name: long-form-precision
    selector:
      - query_length > 200
      - contains_keywords: [calculate, cite, proof, derive]
    action:
      model: athena-9b-f16
      rollout: 100
  - name: chat-default
    selector:
      - query_type: chat
    action:
      model: athena-9b-int8
      rollout: 100
  - name: short-low-risk
    selector:
      - query_length <= 100
      - risk: low
    action:
      model: athena-9b-int6
      rollout: 5 # start small
  - name: canary-mmt
    selector:
      - traffic_pct: 3
    action:
      model: athena-9b-int6
      rollout: 3
metrics_to_watch:
  - slice: long-form-qa
    thresholds:
      rouge_l_delta: -2.0
      hallucination_rate_delta: 0.5
```

Dena L: Nice. For GTN we should expose simple guidance: "Fast but lossy: use int6 for short completions & suggestions; int8 is the balanced default; fallback to f16 for high-precision queries." Add a short blurb on expected cost tradeoffs and the specific slice risks.

Mike R: Ops question — what eval signals do we need in the console? I'd push: per-route ROUGE-L delta, hallucination counters (heuristic), rerank recall@k for retrieval flows, token-level latency p50/p95, effective cache hit rate. Also link eval to prompt-set examples for regression alerts.

Jia W: Quick UX trick — for long queries we can try chunk+stitch (windowed generation) before hitting f16 fallback. In a lot of cases chunking recovers recall and keeps cost down. Also consider soft-fallback: return int6 but attach a flag if confidence low so client can request fallback.

Samir P: Ops note: before enabling routing we'll run a 24h microbench: sample 10k long-form queries, measure delta ROUGE-L, hallucination heuristics, KV-cache reuse, and latency tail. If int6 delta <= -2 ROUGE-L and hallucination delta <= 0.3 we can expand rollout to 20%.

Olivia K: Sounds actionable. Next steps — Samir to run microbench & push canary config, Dena to draft GTN messaging (short guidance + cost table), Mike to wire up the three console signals, Jia to prototype chunking/soft-fallback. We'll reconvene after 24h pilot. :rocket:
